items.t: Called for prefunding the Fire Suppression Fund on an ongoing basis.
items.q: The Governor is particularly concerned about the state’s ability to pay for the upcoming fire season after the Legislature rejected his and the Land Board’s calls for prefunding the Fire Suppression Fund on an ongoing basis

items.t: Said Idaho should never relent in efforts to protect the lives of the preborn.

items.t: Signed Idaho House Bill 37, which designates execution by firing squad as the primary method of execution in Idaho.
items.q: Following the signing of Idaho House Bill 37 into law by Governor Little, which designates execution by firing squad as the primary method of execution in Idaho

items.t: Signed the Fairness in Women's Sports Act (2020).
items.q: The Legislature passed and the Governor signed the “Fairness in Women’s Sports Act” in 2020

items.t: Said Idaho would sue the federal government if necessary to defend his executive order carrying out the Defending Women's Sports Act.
items.q: If necessary, that's what we will do," Little said when asked if his state and Attorney General Raúl R. Labrador would sue the federal government if an incoming Harris administration tried to block his executive order to carry out the Defending Women's Sports Act.

record.t: Signed a bill making the firing squad Idaho's preferred method of execution for capital punishment.
record.q: Idaho Gov. Brad Little signed his name on a bill Wednesday making Idaho the only state in the US to have a firing squad designated as the preferred execution method for capital punishment

record.t: Signed a law making it illegal to help a minor get an abortion by supplying drugs or helping them across state lines without parental consent.
record.q: Idaho Gov. Brad Little signed a law last week that makes it illegal to help a minor get an abortion by supplying them drugs or helping them across state lines to terminate a pregnancy without parental consent.

record.t: Was elected Governor of Idaho in 2018, was reelected in 2022, and has served since January 7, 2019.
record.q: The people of Idaho elected Brad Little to be their Governor in November of 2018 and reelected him in November of 2022. He has served as Idaho’s 33 rd Governor since January 7, 2019.

record.t: Vetoed House Bill 758a, which could eliminate licensing and fire inspection requirements for childcare providers.
record.q: Governor Little vetoed the bill because it threatens child safety. It could eliminate licensing and fire inspection requirements for childcare providers.

record.t: Vetoed House Bill 975, which would put an estimated $50-55 million in the Budget Stabilization Fund.
record.q: Governor Little vetoed the bill because it puts an estimated $50-55 million in the Budget Stabilization Fund (rainy day fund) when the fund is already one of the highest reserve funds in the nation.

record.t: Vetoed House Bill 968, a cash transfers bill.
record.q: The Governor vetoed this bill because the Legislature appropriated funds from canceled Permanent Building Fund (PBF) projects and put it in unrelated accounts.

record.t: Issued an executive order to ban all trans athletes from girls' and women's sports.
record.q: Idaho Republican Governor Brad Little issued an executive order to ban all trans athletes from girls' and women's sports earlier this year

record.t: Issued an executive order targeting illegal voting.
record.q: Idaho Gov. Brad Little issued an executive order targeting illegal voting, which is rare in the state.

record.t: Signed an executive order temporarily suspending state inspections related to dyed diesel fuel.
record.q: Governor Brad Little today signed an executive order temporarily suspending state inspections related to dyed diesel fuel, cutting red tape for Idaho farmers and ranchers during harvest season.

record.t: Announced that Idaho was awarded nearly $183 million in Rural Health Transformation Program funds from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.
record.q: Governor Brad Little announced today the State of Idaho was awarded another nearly $183 million in Rural Health Transformation Program funds from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services
